findings.question: q-physics-work-energy-power-0006
findings.problem: The keyed choice is the only bare outcome; every distractor adds a because clause. For example, a student can select the lone short statement while ignoring how kinetic energy depends on speed.
findings.fix: Give all four choices the same form, such as bare outcomes with no reasons.

findings.question: q-physics-work-energy-power-0009
findings.quote: A has five times B’s power.
findings.problem: The keyed comparison alone has no because clause; all three distractors append reasons. This repeats the format cue in other items, allowing a student to favor this choice without calculating either power.
findings.fix: Use four parallel comparisons without because clauses.

findings.question: q-physics-work-energy-power-0014
findings.quote: Both kinetic and potential energy are positive.
findings.problem: The keyed description alone has no because clause, while every distractor adds one. A student can favor the lone unqualified description without checking the pendulum’s height and motion, especially after seeing the same pattern elsewhere in this file.
findings.fix: Make all four descriptions parallel, either all with reasons or all without them.

findings.question: q-physics-work-energy-power-0019
findings.problem: The keyed prediction is the only bare result; every distractor adds a because clause. The repeated choice-format pattern lets a student favor this answer without understanding potential-energy reference levels.
findings.fix: Use four parallel predictions without reasons, or supply a reason for every choice.
